BY PUBLIC PROSECUTOR SRI.C.M. KAMMAPPU  THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 30-05-2018, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
Revision vs By Advs. Sri.C.S. Dias on 30 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90238128/
1 ma  P.UBAID, J.
 ~~~~~~~~~~
 Crl.R.P No.2090 of 2005  ~~~~~~~~~~~
 Dated this the 30th May, 2018  ORDER

The revision petitioner herein challenges the conviction and sentence against him under Sections 2(ix)
(a) and (c), 7(ii) and 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
This is a case involving mis-branding.
When the Food Inspector demanded a particular article, the retailer sold another article.
To prove the alleged mis- branding, the food article was sent for analysis and report of analysis was received from the Regional Laboratory.
Relying on the report of analysis, the Food Inspector filed complaint before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Attingal.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Attingal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The accused entered appearance and contested the case.
On full trial, he received conviction also.
Aggrieved by the judgment of conviction, he approached the Court of Session, Thiruvananthapuram with Crl.A No.316/1998.
In appeal, the learned II Addl. Sessions Judge, Thiruvananthapuram confirmed the conviction and sentence.
Now the accused is before this Court in revision challenging the legality and propriety of the conviction and sentence.
3. This is a case where the Pepsico decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is applicable.

The position of law now stands settled that in a case where the prosecution relies on the report of analysis to prove a case of adulteration or mis-branding, the report must be from a qualified public analyst of a notified laboratory, and the report must have been made after following the analysis procedure prescribed by the Government by notification.
In this case, the prosecution relies on the report of analysis to prove the case of mis-branding.
This is not a case of mis- branding which can be otherwise proved.
Admittedly, the report was not obtained from a notified laboratory and admittedly the Government has not notified the method of analysis for the food article involved.
In such a situation, the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pepsico's case is very much applicable and the benefit of this must go to the accused.
In the result, this revision petition is allowed.

The revision petitioner is found not guilty of the offence under Sections 2(ix) (a) & (c), 7(ii) and 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and he is acquitted of the said offences in revision.

Accordingly, the conviction and sentence against him in C.C 663/1996 of the court below and confirmed in appeal, will stand set aside, and the revision petitioner will stand released from prosecution.

Sd/-
P.UBAID JUDGE ma /True copy/
